image_description: A man in a boat holds a large sturgeon fish horizontally above the water. The background features a white motorboat, another person standing on the boat, and a forested hillside. The sturgeon is the primary subject, displaying characteristic bony plates and an elongated body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly elongated and the mouth is positioned on the underside (ventral), consistent with sturgeon anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Four distinct barbel structures are visible hanging down from the snout area in front of the mouth.
The snout tapers to a distinct point at the anterior end of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body is long, torpedo-shaped (fusiform), and appears large relative to the human holder.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of raised, bony plates (scutes) are visible along the lateral line and dorsal ridge; no typical fish scales are present.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the fish is dark gray/brown, transitioning to a pale white/cream color on the belly.
The caudal fin is visibly asymmetrical, with the upper lobe being larger and extending further than the lower lobe, a key trait of sturgeons.
